b0: We praise that Śaṃkara, the source of the manifestation of the wheel of Śakti.
Because its nature is unobstructed, there is no destruction anywhere.
The perceiver certainly does not deviate from his own nature.
They clearly exist elsewhere in the continuum of states beginning with pleasure.

source: yadā kṣobhaḥ pralīyeta tadā syātparamaṃ padam
b0: When agitation ceases, then the supreme state is attained.
In the two feet, the all-pervading one shines; elsewhere, He is pure consciousness.

source: sa paśyansatataṃ yukto jīvanmukto na saṃśayaḥ
b0: He who is ever seeing (the Self) and steadfast is a jīvanmukta (liberated while living). There is no doubt.
This is the nirvanic initiation and the bestower of the true nature of Shiva.
Then what is the use of much speaking? It will be understood by itself.
The binder who stands on her own path is known as the bestower of success.
I praise that wonderful speech (or the goddess of speech) which is rich in diverse meanings and beautiful words.
The complete threefold distinction according to the classification of essences from the essence.

source: cakrārūḍham anackaṃ vā kiṃ vā śaktisvarūpakam
b0: Mounted on a wheel, or without a wheel, or indeed the form of Shakti.
Whatever entire form of Bhairava is described.
The state which is full-formed is the Bhairavi of Bhairava's self.
Thus, O Bhairavi, the form of Bhairava is manifested by Bhairavi.

source: krameṇa manaso dārḍhyāt lakṣayet laṣyam uttamam
b0: Through firmness of mind, one should gradually aim at the supreme goal.
Then, from the simultaneous state of non-duality, the non-dual arises.
Through the states of gross, subtle, and supreme, the mind dissolves in the end.
Only the wind-filled one is united with the bliss of love.

source: hoccāraṃ manasā kurvaṃs tataḥ śānte pralīyate
b0: Performing the rising of 'Ha' with the mind, one then dissolves in the Peace.
Through the absence of mental constructs, one is freed from mental constructs.

source: sa evāhaṃ śaivadharmā iti dārḍhyāc chivo bhavet
b0: By firmness in the thought "I myself am the Shaiva dharma," one becomes Shiva.
The Tarkasamgraha is composed for the easy understanding of children.
There, the substances are nine: earth, water, fire, air, ether, time, space, soul, and mind.

Form, taste, smell, touch, number, dimension, individuality, conjunction, disjunction, priority, posteriority, gravity, fluidity, viscidity, sound, intellect, pleasure, pain, desire, aversion, effort, merit, demerit, and impressions are the twenty-four qualities.
But inherence is only one.
Non-existence is fourfold: prior non-existence, posterior non-existence, absolute non-existence, and mutual non-existence.

source: śabdaguṇam ākāśam / tac caikaṃ vibhu nityaṃ ca
b0: Space has the quality of sound, and it is one, all-pervading, and eternal.

source: sukhādyupalabdhisādhanam indriyaṃ manaḥ / tac ca pratyātmaniyatatvād anantaṃ paramāṇurūpaṃ nityaṃ ca
b0: The mind is the instrument for the perception of pleasure, etc. And because it is confined to each individual self, it is infinite, atomic in form, and eternal.

source: tvagindriyamātragrāhyo guṇo saparśaḥ / sa ca trividhaḥ śitoṣṇānuṣṇāśītabhedāt / pṛthivyaptejovāyuvṛttiḥ / tatra śīto jale / uṣṇas tejasi / anuṣṇāśītaḥ pṛthivīvāyvoḥ
b0: The quality of touch is perceived only by the skin. It is of three kinds, based on the distinction of cold, hot, and temperate. It resides in earth, water, fire, and air. Among these, cold is in water, hot in fire, and temperate in earth and air.

source: mānavyavahārakāraṇaṃ parimāṇaṃ / navadravyavṛtti / tac caturvidham / aṇu mahad dīrghaṃ hrasvaṃ ceti
b0: Measurement is the cause of the practical usage of measures. It inheres in nine substances. It is fourfold: atomic, large, long, and short.

source: sa dvividho yathārtho 'yathārthaś ca / tadvati tatprakārako 'nubhavo yathārthaḥ / yathā rajata idaṃ rajatam iti jñānam / sa eva pramety ucyate / tadabhāvavati tatprakārako 'nubhavo 'yathārthaḥ / yathā śuktāv idaṃ rajatam iti jñānam
b0: That is of two kinds: valid and invalid. The cognition whose qualifier corresponds to a locus that truly possesses it is valid. For example, the cognition "this is silver" (with respect to actual silver). That itself is called valid cognition (*pramā*). The cognition whose qualifier corresponds to a locus devoid of it is invalid. For example, the cognition "this is silver" with respect to a (pearl) shell.
The sapakṣa is that which possesses the sādhya definitely, as for example the kitchen itself.
When each subsequent cause (among suffering, birth, activity, defect, and false knowledge) ceases, the preceding effect ceases; and from the cessation of that preceding effect, liberation results.
